summary: Nucleum is a dense economic euro where players build rail and power-line networks across a map to deliver energy from nuclear plants to cities, while climbing a shared tech tree and using an action-retrieval mechanism (columns of action tiles that shift and get replaced) to plan efficient turns. Turns are engine-building puzzles with tight resource conversion, heavy multi-turn planning, and constant tension between expanding your network, upgrading buildings, and racing others to key tech and map spots.
praised: Satisfying, tightly interlocking engine-building puzzle with a strong sense of progression
Action-retrieval system creates interesting tactical tension each round
Good component quality and thematic production for a euro
Multiple viable strategies and replayability from variable setup/tech paths
criticised: Very heavy rules overhead and long teach for a first game
Significant downtime in multiplayer as turns require deep calculation
Some randomness in tile/action availability feels at odds with the otherwise tight optimization
Map/network building can feel a bit disconnected from the tech-tree half of the game
Not much direct player interaction beyond space/route competition

interaction.kind: indirect competition for map spots, routes, and tech track positions

scoring.why: Points accumulate from network size, power plant upgrades, tech track advancement, contracts, and end-game bonuses, rewarding a well-rounded engine over one narrow strategy
